## Cutoff sensitivity

The two zone cutoffs are the only fitted values in the policy layer
([5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-pd-zones)), so they are the first thing a validator moves. Each
scenario moves one cutoff by {{< var adj.sens.step >}} of its value, leaves everything else
as committed — the model, its PDs, every knockout and override — and re-runs `decide` on the
held-out applicants (`wiki/facts/adj_facts.py`):

```python
c2 = replace(cfg, **{field: getattr(cfg, field) * factor})     # wiki/facts/adj_facts.py
d2 = decide(X_all.iloc[te], p_te, c2)["decision"].to_numpy()
```

{{< include ../../_generated/adj-cutoffs.md >}}

Decision mix and changed files are on the {{< var adj.n_test >}} held-out applicants. The
last row is not a sensitivity scenario; it is the evidence for finding 4 and is read there.

## Reading the table

**The decisions barely move.** Moving `t_low` by {{< var adj.sens.step >}} either way
changes {{< var adj.sens.t_low_down.changed >}} and {{< var adj.sens.t_low_up.changed >}}
held-out decisions; moving `t_high` changes {{< var adj.sens.t_high_down.changed >}} (down)
and {{< var adj.sens.t_high_up.changed >}} (up). No decision share moves by as much as a percentage point. Two reasons, both from the
code:

- **The knockouts absorb the Decline edge.** Most Declines are knockouts
  ([5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-knockouts-dominate)), and a knockout Decline does not depend on
  `t_high` at all. Moving `t_high` reaches only the files in the narrow band of PDs around
  it that carry no knockout.
- **The overrides absorb part of the Approve edge.** A file that `t_low` moves into the
  Approve zone is still referred if its coverage is thin or its score is under the floor;
  only the files that pass every override and every knockout change decision.

**What this does and does not establish.** The decisions are robust to a modest error in
either cutoff, so the in-sample quantiles behind them ([5.4](assumptions.qmd#adj-thresholds-are-quantiles))
do little damage on this data. The same robustness is a reminder of what
[5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-knockouts-dominate) found: the policy layer, not the PD, decides
most of the Declines, so a stress test of this component is mainly a stress test of its
rules.

## Policy limits

The other seven policy values are not varied in the facts. Two of them could be moved a long
way without any effect, because they never fire (finding 2, [5.7](limitations.qmd)). The
v2 loan workbench lets a reviewer move any of the nine values and see the decision for one
file, and how many decisions flip across the whole book (`flipped_count`), recomputed by the
same `decide` the batch uses ([5.1](purpose.qmd#who-consumes-it-and-how)). It is the tool
for exploring a limit; this chapter records only the cutoff scenarios, which are fixed in
code and rerun identically by `python verify.py`.

## Reduced-input refits: not run

D4 refits the scorecard on reduced inputs and documents a gate failure when the bureau feed
is down (D4.6). No such refit is run for adjudication. What can be said without one:

- **The bureau feed reaches adjudication twice**: through its own bureau columns
  ([5.2](data.qmd#adj-features)) and through the score, which loses its gate without them
  (D4.6). An adjudication model refitted without the bureau is therefore not the validated
  model either, and the documented response is the same as D4's: refer an applicant whose
  bureau data are missing to an underwriter.
- **As the code stands, a missing value is not referred.** A missing numeric feature becomes
  zero in `compute_adjudication_features`, and `decide` also fills a missing `dscr`, leverage,
  public-records or delinquency value with zero (a missing `business_score` takes the score
  floor, and revenue is floored at 1). A zero `dscr` is a knockout: a file with a missing coverage
  ratio would be declined for `dscr` below the floor, with a reason that is not true
  ([5.7](limitations.qmd#adj-observations)).

A reduced-input refit, with the score recomputed from the same reduced inputs, is listed for
the next redevelopment ([5.8](monitoring.qmd#adj-redevelopment-triggers)).
